Production clients are Rc-backed and these fields observe them. Preserve null/absent and CLIENT_DEAD behavior, hold an upgrade guard during access, and release guards at deliberate boundaries. Client loss closes TTY, stops control and clears format jobs before deferred final release; rejecting all back-pointers merely because they cannot be references was too broad. Erased window.latest is assigned client addresses only. Evidence: src/server_client.rs client::new, server_client_lost, server_client_free; src/format/jobs.rs format_lost_client; src/cmd/queue.rs target-client selection; src/input.rs input_init/input_add_request; src/monitor.rs monitor_create_client.

These fields do not own a session reference, but production sessions are Rc-backed. Weak observers avoid adding ownership. Upgrade for access and separately validate active registry membership/session logical state: deferred destruction can leave an allocation alive after removal. Handle reassignment/group moves explicitly; remove conflicting test fixtures rather than treating them as a production ownership rule. Evidence: src/session.rs session_create, session_destroy, session_remove_ref, session_group_remove; src/server_client.rs server_client_set_session; src/window_panes.rs initialization.

A persistent borrow is not required. Evidence: src/window.rs winlink_add, winlink_weak, winlink_remove, winlinks_reindex; src/shared/window.rs winlinks.
